an4.38:1.1: “Monks, a monk who has shaken off idiosyncratic truths [pacceka-sacca], who has thoroughly given up searching, who is calmed in his bodily fabrication, is said to be detached.
an4.38:1.2: “And how has a monk shaken off idiosyncratic truths?
an4.38:1.3: There is the case where a monk has shaken off the run-of-the-mill idiosyncratic truths of run-of-the-mill contemplatives & brahmans—in other words,
an4.38:1.4: ‘The cosmos is eternal,’ ‘The cosmos is not eternal,’ ‘The cosmos is finite,’ ‘The cosmos is infinite,’ ‘The soul & the body are the same,’ ‘The soul is one thing and the body another,’ ‘After death a Tathāgata exists,’ ‘After death a Tathāgata does not exist,’ ‘After death a Tathāgata both does & does not exist,’ ‘After death a Tathāgata neither does nor does not exist.’
an4.38:1.5: All of these he has thrown off, shaken off, renounced, vomited up, let go, abandoned, relinquished.
an4.38:1.6: This is how a monk has shaken off idiosyncratic truths.
an4.38:2.1: “And how has a monk thoroughly given up searching?
an4.38:2.2: There is the case where a monk has abandoned his search for sensuality, has abandoned his search for becoming, and has allayed his search for a holy life.
an4.38:2.3: This is how a monk has thoroughly given up searching.
an4.38:3.1: “And how is a monk calmed in his bodily fabrication?
an4.38:3.2: There is the case where a monk, with the abandoning of pleasure & pain—as with the earlier disappearance of elation & distress—enters & remains in the fourth jhāna: purity of equanimity & mindfulness, neither pleasure nor pain.
an4.38:3.3: This is how a monk is calmed in his bodily fabrication.
an4.38:4.2: There is the case where a monk’s conceit, ‘I am,’ is abandoned, its root destroyed, made like a palmyra stump, deprived of the conditions of development, not destined for future arising.
an4.38:4.3: This is how a monk is detached.”
an4.38:5.3: i.e., grasping at ‘such is the truth’
an4.38:5.4: based on an accumulation of viewpoints:
